This is a /simplify review (code QUALITY, not correctness bugs) of uncommitted changes in /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim. Theme: a new C++ driver (F6 "phase-plan executor") was added, and the "vsim -> QEMU2 handback" leg was removed repo-wide (mostly deletions).

YOUR ANGLE: ALTITUDE. Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure signal the fix isn't deep enough -- prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding special cases.

SCOPE (review only these CODE files; IGNORE all *.md docs):
NEW code -- Read the whole files:
  driver/argv.cpp, driver/argv.hpp, driver/plan.hpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
  driver/run_plan.hpp, driver/plan_test.cpp, driver/plan_itest.cpp
MODIFIED -- `git diff HEAD -- <file>` (or `git -C verilator diff -- <file>`):
  driver/engine_registry.cpp, driver/CMakeLists.txt
  tools/orchestrator/{runner.py,checkpoint.py,main.py}
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_*.c (7 files)
  verilator/src/hybrid/{csr_trigger,resume_driver,state_drain,v_regfile_xfer}.hpp

Look especially for:
- The F6 design: is the qemu "fast-leg" invoke template hardcoded in engine_registry.cpp builtin_qemu() at the right altitude, or should it live with argv.cpp's templating? Is the split between plan_argvs (pure) and run_plan (spawns) the right seam, or a leaky one?
- The fixture DCE-anchoring (rt_c_v_regs stores y to a static y_out; rt_c_v_matmul adds a markerless "memory" barrier; matmul/static_buf rely on exit_vsim's clobber): is this a consistent general anchor, or 3 different per-fixture special-cases for the same problem? Would a shared anchor helper in runtime/rt_c_helpers.h be the right depth?
- checkpoint.py / main.py / runner.py replay: after dropping `--resume-with qemu`, is the `model` parameter now a vestigial single-value axis that should collapse, or is keeping it right?
- Does run_plan special-case anything that the EngineDescriptor/invoke mechanism should handle generically?

The orchestrator/vsim changes are mostly DELETIONS -- judge whether what REMAINS sits at the right altitude after the removal.

First read the scope files, then report. Each finding: `file:line` + one-line summary + the deeper/more-general form. If the depth is right, say so. Do NOT report correctness bugs. Do NOT touch docs.

1	// Placeholder substitution for engine invoke templates -- the template-driven
2	// port of orchestrator/spawn.py (minus QEMU2). spawn.py hand-built each argv in
3	// Python; here the argv *shape* lives in each engine's `invoke` template (from
4	// `--describe`, see docs/engine_interface.md) and build_argv fills the
5	// {placeholders} from a context map. The framework thus keeps zero per-engine
6	// argv code: a new engine ships its own template.
7	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
8	#define ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
9	
10	#include <map>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <vector>
13	
14	namespace andes_sim {
15	
16	// Substitute every "{key}" in `tmpl`'s args with `ctx.at(key)`. A key may
17	// appear anywhere in an arg (so "mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}" expands in
18	// one arg) and more than once. Recognised keys come from `ctx`; a "{key}" with
19	// no matching ctx entry is an error (returns {} and sets `err`). On success
20	// `err` is cleared and the fully-resolved argv is returned.
21	std::vector<std::string> build_argv(const std::vector<std::string>& tmpl,
22	                                    const std::map<std::string, std::string>& ctx,
23	                                    std::string& err);
24	
25	}  // namespace andes_sim
26	
27	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
28

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
31	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
32	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
33	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
34	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
35	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
36	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
37	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
38	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
39	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
40	
41	struct PlanOptions {
42	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
43	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
44	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
45	};
46	
47	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
48	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
49	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
50	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
51	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
52	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
53	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
54	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
55	
56	}  // namespace andes_sim
57	
58	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
59

3	 * Phase rule:
4	 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
5	 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,

8	 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted

12	 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
13	 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.

20	 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
21	 *
22	 * CSR mode pattern-matches the csrwi insns directly; the helpers do not
23	 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
24	 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
25	 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
26	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
27	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
28	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
29	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
30	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
31	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
32	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
33	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
34	/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
35	 *
36	 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
37	 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
38	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
39	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
40	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
41	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
42	 * consumes the value.)
43	 *
44	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
45	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
46	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
47	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
48	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
49	 *     between the markers.

51	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is

55	 * attribution. */

"""Subprocess factories for QEMU and vsim.

argv builders are pure (no I/O), so they unit-test cleanly. The actual
process spawn goes through `subprocess.Popen` directly in `runner.py`.

The flow is 2-phase: QEMU 1 drains on the plugin trigger, vsim resumes and
drains. There is no QEMU 2 leg -- the vsim -> QEMU2 handback was removed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path


def qemu_drain_argv(qemu_bin: Path, elf: Path, plugin: Path,
                    mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
                    state_out: Path) -> list[str]:
    """QEMU 1: load ELF, drain on plugin's CSR/PC trigger, exit 200."""
    mem_obj = (
        f"memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,"
        f"mem-path={mmap_path},size={mmap_size}"
    )
    return [
        str(qemu_bin),
        "-object", mem_obj,
        "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem",
        "-cpu", "andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512",
        "-nographic",
        "-semihosting-config", "enable=on,target=native",
        "-bios", str(elf),
        "-plugin", f"{plugin},outfile={state_out}",
    ]


def vsim_argv(vsim_bin: Path, elf: Path,
              state_in: Path, state_out: Path,
              mmap_path: Path, mmap_size: int,
              shared_mem_base: int = 0x00000000) -> list[str]:
    """vsim: resume from QEMU 1 state, run ROI, drain, exit 200.

    vsim drains and exits; the cycle figure is its mcycle delta. There is
    no in-process QEMU spawn (the handback was removed).
    """
    return [
        str(vsim_bin),
        str(elf),
        "--resume-from-qemu", str(state_in),
        "--handoff-out", str(state_out),
        "--shared-mem-path", str(mmap_path),
        "--shared-mem-size", str(mmap_size),
        "--shared-mem-base", hex(shared_mem_base),
    ]

def replay_checkpoint(
    snap_dir: Path,
    *,
    model: str,
    project_root: Path,
    work_dir: Path,
    artifacts=None,
    spawn_timeout: float = 90.0,
):
    """Hydrate a snap_dir/ archive and resume the chosen model.

    Validates `meta.json` via `validate_replay_meta`, allocates a fresh
    /dev/shm mmap sized to `meta.mem_size`, overwrites it with
    `snap_dir/mem`, copies `snap_dir/state.bin` into `work_dir` as the
    spawn's `state_in`, then drives a synthetic 1-step `Session` through
    `runner.run_session()` with `initial_state_in` pointing at the copy.

    `model='vsim'` -> 1-step `(vsim, csr)` plan; vsim resumes from
                      state_in, executes the ROI, drains on its CSR-exit
                      trigger, exits 200. vsim is the only supported model
                      (the QEMU2 resume path was removed).

    Returns the `SessionResult` from `run_session()` unchanged;
    `state_paths` has exactly one entry (the drained state).
    """
    from orchestrator.mmap_owner import MmapOwner
    from orchestrator.plan import Session, Step, TriggerSpec
    from orchestrator.runner import Artifacts, run_session

    meta = json.loads((snap_dir / "meta.json").read_text())
    artifacts = artifacts or Artifacts.from_env(project_root)
    live_cpu_variant = _cpu_variant_from_vsim_path(artifacts.vsim)
    validate_replay_meta(meta, live_cpu_variant=live_cpu_variant)

    mem_size = int(meta["mem_size"])
    elf_path = str(meta["elf_path"])

    work_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    state_in = work_dir / "replay-state-in.bin"
    shutil.copy(snap_dir / "state.bin", state_in)

    if model != "vsim":
        raise ValueError(
            f"unsupported replay model: {model!r} "
            f"(only 'vsim' is supported; the QEMU2 resume path was removed)"
        )
    trigger_kind = "csr"

    with MmapOwner.allocate(mem_size) as shm:
        shutil.copy(snap_dir / "mem", shm.path)
        synth = Session(
            elf=elf_path,
            mem_size=mem_size,
            mmap_path=str(shm.path),
            steps=(Step(
                model=model,
                trigger=TriggerSpec(kind=trigger_kind, params={}),
            ),),
        )
        return run_session(
            synth, project_root,
            artifacts=artifacts, spawn_timeout=spawn_timeout,
            work_dir=work_dir,
            initial_state_in=state_in,
        )


def _cpu_variant_from_vsim_path(vsim_bin: Path) -> str | None:
    name = vsim_bin.name
    if name.startswith("sim_"):
        return name[len("sim_"):]
    return None

## Code-quality review (altitude angle) -- uncommitted driver/orchestrator/fixture changes

Verdict up front: the C++ F6 core is at the right depth; the Python-side handback removal is mostly thorough but leaves one half-removed concept (`end_of_program`) and one vestigial single-value axis (`replay --resume-with`).

### Q1 -- F6 template + plan_argvs/run_plan seam: RIGHT depth, no change
- `driver/engine_registry.cpp:40-47` -- the qemu `fast-leg` template living in `builtin_qemu()` is the correct altitude, NOT something for `argv.cpp`. The invoke template belongs to the engine descriptor; QEMU's descriptor is built-in only because QEMU has no `--describe` (vsim ships the identical-shaped template via `--describe`). `argv.cpp` is the engine-agnostic `{placeholder}` fill mechanism and correctly knows nothing about QEMU's argv shape. Moving the template into `argv.cpp` would re-introduce per-engine argv code into the framework core -- the exact thing `--describe` exists to delete.
- `driver/run_plan.cpp` -- the pure `plan_argvs` / spawning `run_plan` split is a clean seam, not leaky. `plan_argvs` takes an already-resolved `RuntimeCtx` + `workdir` and returns argvs; `run_plan` owns mmap/workdir/spawn/readback. Both sides derive drain paths from the same pure `state_path()` helper (`run_plan.cpp:21`), so the threading convention can't drift between fill and readback. Right seam.

### Q2 -- fixture DCE-anchoring: ONE consistent anchor (right), except one extractable raw-asm barrier
The three fixtures are not 3 unrelated special-cases -- they are the single documented idiom (`rt_c_helpers.h:34-55`: write the kernel output to memory inside the ROI; `exit_vsim`'s `"memory"` clobber pins the store) applied at the natural granularity:
- matmul / static_buf: kernel already stores to `.bss`; `exit_vsim` anchors it -> zero new code (deepest form).
- `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.c:47,72` -- new `static y_out[]` + `vse32` store inside the ROI is the SAME idiom; the store is new only because that output was register-only (previously consumed in QEMU2). A shared helper can't know what/where to store, so this is correctly the workload's own concern. Right depth.

The one outlier worth deepening:
- `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c:100` -- the markerless branch hand-rolls `__asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory")`, which is exactly `exit_vsim()` minus the `csrwi`. Deeper/more-general form: add a named `roi_anchor()` to `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h` that emits the bare clobber, and define `exit_vsim()` as `roi_anchor()` + the `csrwi`. That removes the duplicated raw-asm idiom and gives the markerless anchor a name instead of an unexplained inline barrier.

### Q3 -- `model` axis after dropping `--resume-with qemu`: SPLIT verdict
- `runner.py` `model`: keep. Still two real values (`qemu` drain, `vsim` drain), both live in `_execute_step`. Not vestigial.
- Replay path `model`: collapse it. `main.py:94` declares `--resume-with` as `choices=("vsim",)` -- a one-element choice -- and `checkpoint.py:233` guards `if model != "vsim": raise`. The `replay_checkpoint(model=...)` kwarg now always equals `"vsim"`, so the guard and `Step(model=model)` are dead generality. Deeper form: drop the `--resume-with` flag and the `model` kwarg entirely, hardcode `"vsim"` in the synthetic `Step`. (A one-choice flag is a textbook vestigial axis; matches the "no future-proofing" rule.)

### Q4 -- run_plan special-casing the descriptor should own: mild/latent
- `driver/run_plan.cpp:144,150` -- `run_plan` hardcodes `expect_rc == 200` and unconditionally `read_state_file` for every step, i.e. it bakes in the "every leg drains" contract rather than deriving the per-step success contract from `EngineDescriptor.state` / `result` (which already model exactly this). Acceptable today because F6 is drain-only by design, but the descriptor fields exist precisely so a non-drain leg (e.g. a `standalone` run) wouldn't need new code in `run_plan`. Right for now; flag the latent coupling.

### Cross-cutting -- the handback deletion is thorough EXCEPT `end_of_program` is half-removed
Clean deletions (good altitude): `gdbstub.py` is gone (no orphan), `spawn.py` is down to 51 lines (`qemu_resume_argv`/`pick_free_port` removed), and `runner.resume_qemu_from_state` / `_qemu_resume_to_end` / `main.py qemu-resume` are gone with no dangling imports.

But the `end_of_program` trigger kind is only half-removed -- `runner.py` now rejects it at runtime (`raise ValueError(unsupported (model=qemu, trigger=...))`) while it still survives as live vocabulary:
- In-scope stale docstrings: `tools/orchestrator/runner.py:50` ("Resume-and-finish steps (trigger `end_of_program`)...") and `:199` ("the input to a drain or end_of_program spawn") describe a path the same file now refuses.
- Out-of-scope debris confirming the removal is shallow: `examples/csr_oneshot.yaml:21` is now an unrunnable example (3rd step is `end_of_program`; runner rejects it) whose header still says "QEMU2 resumes + runs to workload completion"; `plan.py:15-22` still lists `end_of_program` in the trigger vocabulary; `tests/test_main_dry_run.py:30` still asserts on it.

Deeper form: retire `end_of_program` as a trigger kind everywhere it appears (it is now an unrunnable word), or at minimum scrub the two in-scope `runner.py` docstrings so the file stops advertising a capability it deletes.
